subject: Re: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA & Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Alexa Donovan <alexa.donovan@finware.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finware.com>; legal@finware.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA/Order Form redlines

Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move to procurement for the Private deployment (VPC-hosted in our AWS account), our legal team has circulated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form focused on: deployment rights, license scope (ability to run on our infra), audit/certification evidence, and options for continuity in the event of vendor insolvency.

I attach the redlines and an internal note summarizing their asks (high level):
- Explicit license to run Redwood runtime and model artifacts for inference on our VPC (limited to production servers listed in Exhibit A).
- Right to retain a copy of the model bundle and runtime if Redwood ceases to operate (they call this a de facto "escrow").
- On-site audit right once per year and access to logs related to data handling & access controls.
- Proof of SOC 2 + snapshot of recent audit logs and change-control records.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept any of these as-is, and if not, propose alternative language? We are under a tight timeline to close before year-end.

Attachments: FinWare_redlines_MSA.docx (docx)

—Alexa
Alexa Donovan
Head of Procurement, FinWare Inc.
alexa.donovan@finware.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Donovan <alexa.donovan@finware.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA/Order Form redlines

Alexa —

Appreciate the redlines. Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Ava (customer success / infra handoff) to ensure we align legal and operationally. Quick responses to the bullets you outlined: 

- License to run on your VPC: Yes, Redwood supports Private deployments and we can grant an inference-only runtime license scoped to the deployment in Exhibit A. We need to nail the exact nodes and any dev/staging vs production separation.

- Copy of model bundle / escrow: This is the tricky bit. Our standard position is we do not provide model weights or source code under a customer escrow — models are third-party or trained IP, and releasing weights raises IP and safety concerns. That said, we can propose a continuity alternative: (1) deposit runtime container images and runtime artifacts into a controlled escrow (no model weights), (2) provide an emergency runtime access plan (time-limited credentials and signed SLA triggers) that allows you to continue inference for a transitional period, and (3) negotiate a defined process for a court/receivership release with strict usage limits.

- On-site audit: we can support audits focused on our control plane evidence and data handling practices; for Private deployments where the control plane is customer-managed, we can provide SOC 2 documentation, audit logs export, and an onsite/remote audit with reasonable notice.

- Proof of SOC2 / logs: attaching our SOC2 summary and a proposed list of logs we can export. Ava — can you confirm the practical list of artifacts we can hand over for a customer audit?

Proposed next steps: Marissa to draft redline counter for the MSA + addendum that captures the inference-only license, a narrowly scoped escrow alternative, and an audit evidence bundle. Can we set a 30-minute call next week to resolve legal points?

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Donovan <alexa.donovan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA/Order Form redlines

Alexa / team —

Thanks for sharing the redlines. Please find an initial Redwood counter embedded in the attached addendum (Redwood_proposed_addendum_v1.docx). Highlights / rationale: 

1) License scope — We will grant an inference-only license to run the Redwood runtime and associated deployment artifacts within FinWare's VPC for the environment and node count defined in Exhibit A. This license explicitly prohibits extraction, replication, or distribution of model weights or underlying model parameters.

2) Escrow / continuity — We cannot place model weights into escrow. Instead we propose: 
   - Deposit of signed runtime container image(s) and deployment manifests into an independent escrow agent; these images will not include model weights.
   - A transition support clause: upon a defined trigger (Redwood insolvency or failure to support per an SLA), Redwood (or the escrow agent under strict instructions) will provide time-limited access to runtime images and a copy of the last known configuration + encrypted KMS-wrapped keys. Any use is restricted to continuing inference for a defined period (90 days) and limited to the environment specified in Exhibit A.

3) Audits — We agree to yearly audits with reasonable notice. For Private deployments, we will provide: SOC 2 summary, audit logs export (access/control/changes), and evidence of change-control for runtime artifacts. On-site audits will be scoped and limited to avoid exposing Redwood IP.

4) Evidence package — Attached is a checklist of artifacts we can provide and suggested redline language to replace your escrow ask.

If FinWare legal is okay with that structure I think we have a path to close. If not, please indicate which of the three elements (model weights, escrow possession, unrestricted audit) you view as non-negotiable so we can route appropriately inside Redwood.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: runtime-artifact-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alexa Donovan <alexa.donovan@finware.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@finware.com>; legal@finware.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA/Order Form redlines

Marissa —

Thank you — that clarifies a lot and the approach is reasonable in principle. A couple of items we still need clarified from our counsel: 

- FinWare's core concern is business continuity for inference in a worst-case vendor insolvency scenario. Our legal team will push hard on either: (A) model weights in escrow, or (B) a guaranteed mechanism to replicate model behavior within our environment. They view runtime images without weights as insufficient unless accompanied by an acceptance test / golden-output verification and an explicit transfer mechanism.

- Regarding the KMS-wrapped keys: can you confirm who holds the unwrapping keys and what thresholds apply for release? Our security team needs assurance that keys are under an escrow agent or joint control to prevent unilateral access.

We can accept an initial 90-day transitional window but need clearer acceptance criteria (how will FinWare validate that the runtime in escrow will provide equivalent inference quality?). If you can add a short acceptance test spec (example prompt/response checks) to the addendum, that will help.

Also proposing a 30-minute legal-to-legal call on Wed Dec 2 at 10am PT to triage remaining points. Can you confirm availability?

—Alexa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Donovan <alexa.donovan@finware.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FinWare Private Deployment — MSA/Order Form redlines

Alexa / team —

Thanks — we can do the Dec 2, 10am PT legal call. Confirming next steps from Redwood: 

1) Legal (Marissa) will incorporate an acceptance-test annex into the addendum (simple deterministic prompt/response checks and tolerance thresholds) and the proposed escrow language (runtime images + manifests + KMS-wrapped keys under third-party escrow).

2) Product/CS (Ava) will prepare the evidence package to share pre-call: SOC2 summary, list of exportable audit logs, recent change-control records, and a sample golden-output test set.

3) Security to clarify key custody options — we can discuss joint-custody vs escrow-agent-only key release mechanics on the call.

Please confirm if you want a 45-minute slot instead of 30 given there are several technical points. I've created a HubSpot record and attached the relevant docs for your counsel.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/fw-2026-047
Attachments on our side: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Appreciate the patience — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
